$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{q}=\int \mathrm{idt} \\ & \int_0^2(0.02 \mathrm{t}+0.01) \mathrm{dt}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{q}=\left[0.02 \frac{\mathrm{t}^2}{2}+0.01 \mathrm{t}\right]_1^2 \\ & =0.01(3)+0.01(1) \\ & =0.04 \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two sources of equal emfs are connected in series. This combination is connected to an external resistance $R$. The internal resistances of the two sources are ${r}_{1}$ and ${r}_{2}  \left({r}_{1}> {r}_{2}\right)$. If the potential difference across the source of internal resistance ${r}_{1}$ is zero then the value of $R will be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Current through the wire will be,

$I = \dfrac{2ε}{R + {r}_{1} + {r}_{2}}$.

Now potential difference across cell~$1$~will be,~$ε - I{r}_{1} = 0$

$⇒ ε = \dfrac{2ε}{R + {r}_{1} + {r}_{2}} \times {r}_{1} ⇒ R + {r}_{1} + {r}_{2} = 2{r}_{1} ⇒ R = {r}_{1} - {r}_{2}$

questions.q: The resistance per centimeter of a meter bridge wire is $r$, with $XΩ$ resistance in left gap. Balancing length from left end is at $40$ cm with $25Ω$ resistance in right gap. Now the wire is replaced by another wire of $2r$ resistance per centimeter. The new balancing length for same settings will be at
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For first case:

$\dfrac{X}{r{l}_{1}} = \dfrac{25}{r{l}_{2}}$ ... (i)

For second case:

$\dfrac{X}{\left(2r\right)l^{'}1} = \dfrac{25}{\left(2r\right)l{'}_{2}}$ ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii), we get

$\dfrac{l{'}_{1}}{l1} = \dfrac{l{'}_{2}}{{l}_{2}}$ also total length is constant.

Therefore, balance length doesn't change and

$l{'}_{1} = {l}_{1} = 40cm$

questions.q: A moving coil galvanometer, having a resistance $G,$ produces full scale deflection when a current ${I}_{G}$ flows through it. This galvanometer can be converted into (i) an ammeter of range 0 to ${I}_{o}  \left({I}_{0}> {I}_{g}\right)$ by connecting a shunt resistance ${R}_{A}$ to it and (ii) into a voltmeter of range 0 to $V  \left(V = G{I}_{0}\right)$ by connecting a series resistance ${R}_{V}$ to it. Then,
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$For ammeter: \left({I}_{0} - {I}_{G}\right) \times {R}_{A} = {I}_{G} \times G ⇒ {I}_{0} = {I}_{G} \times \dfrac{ \left(G + {R}_{A}\right)}{{R}_{A}}$
For voltmeter: ${V}_{0} = {I}_{G}\left(G + {R}_{V}\right)$
$∵ {V}_{0} = {I}_{0} \timesG$
$⇒ {I}_{G} \times \left(G + {R}_{V}\right) = {I}_{G} \times $\dfrac{\left(G + {R}_{A}\right) \times G}{{R}_{A}}
$⇒ {R}_{A} \timesG + {R}_{V} \times {R}_{A} =G^{2} + {R}_{A} \timesG$
$⇒ {R}_{V}{R}_{A} = G^{2}$
Again, $\dfrac{{R}_{A}}{{R}_{V}} = \dfrac{{I}_{G} \times G}{{I}_{0} - {I}_{G}} \times \dfrac{{I}_{G}}{\left({I}_{0} - {I}_{G}\right) \times G} = \dfrac{{{I}_{G}}^{2}}{{\left({I}_{0} - {I}_{G}\right)}^{2}}$

options: Drift from higher potential to lower potential&
Move with the uniform velocity throughout from lower potential to higher potential
Move in the straight line paths in the same direction&
Move in the curved paths from lower potential to higher potential

questions.solution:
The electrons inside the conductor move with an average velocity due to the applied field in a direction opposite to the field, this velocity is known as drift velocity.& Electric field are applied from high to low potential region of the conductor. Also, electrons are negatively charged.

Electron drifts from lower potential to higher potential on curved path.

questions.q: A wire of resistance $160 Ω$& is melted and drawn in a wire of one-fourth of its length. The new resistance of the wire will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the resistance of the original wire is given by

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{A} . . . \left(1\right)$

When the new wire is formed, its resistance is given by

$R ' = ρ$\dfrac{l '}{4A} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the expression for the new resistance.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{R '}{R}& = & \dfrac{ρ\dfrac{l '}{4A}}{ρ\dfrac{l}{A}}\\ & ⇒ & R ' = R\dfrac{l '}{4l} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required new resistance.

$\begin{cases}R ' & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{l}{4}}{4l} \times160Ω \\ & = & 10Ω\end{cases}$$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : The equivalent emf of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than either of the two emfs.
Statement-II : The equivalent internal resistance of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than the internal resistance of either of the two batteries.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In parallel connections
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{1}{r_1}+\frac{1}{r_2} \\
& \frac{E_{\mathrm{eq}}}{r_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{E_1}{r_1}+\frac{E_2}{r_2}
\end{aligned}$
If $E_1=E_2$ and $r_1=r_2, E_{\text {eq }}=E_1=E_2\therefore$ Statement 1 is false.
$r_{\text {eq }}$ is less then both $r_1$ and $r_2\therefore$ Statement II is true

questions.q:
A hollow cylindrical conductor has length of $3 . 14m$, while its inner and outer diameters are $4$ mm and $8$ mm respectively. The resistance of the conductor is $n \times {10}^{- 3}Ω$.
If the resistivity of the material is $2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of a conductor with uniform cross-section is given by,

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{A}$

In this case~the cross-sectional area is $\pi \left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)$.

Therefore,

$R = ρ$\dfrac{l}{\pi\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\left(2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 8}\right) \times 3 . 14}{3 . 14 \times \left[\left({4}^{2} - {2}^{2}\right) \times {10}^{- 6}\right]} =$2 \times {10}^{- 3}Ω$

Hence,~$n = 2.

$

questions.q:
Current measured by the ammeter \left(A\right)$ in the reported circuit when no current flows through $10Ω$ resistance, will be _____~$A$.

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
This is a Wheatstone circuit. For the current to be zero in& $10Ω$ the Wheatstone circuit should be balanced. Therefore,

$\dfrac{R}{3} = \dfrac{4}{6} ⇒ R = 2Ω$

Now, the equivalent resistance across the battery will be,~

${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{\left(2 + 4\right) \times \left(3 + 6\right)}{\left(2 + 4\right) + \left(3 + 6\right)} = 3 . 6Ω$

Therefore, the current measured by the ammeter is~$i = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{36}{3 . 6} = 10A$.
